basis: Congenital muscular dystrophy with defining brain and eye malformations; retinal dysplasia in 2/4. Renal dysplasia in 1/4 is below threshold.
Retinal dystrophy, microcornea, cataracts and posterior staphyloma; explicitly lacks systemic features.
Inflammatory vitreous disease within the uveitis spectrum; infectious or immune-mediated ocular inflammation.
Congenital cutaneous Langerhans-cell histiocytic proliferation; skin lesions define this usually self-resolving variant. Systemic damage is uncommon.
Congenital bilateral finger overgrowth defines a structural limb disorder.
Testicular germ-cell malignancy arises in a reproductive organ; no established common damage to an included axis.
Pulmonary tuberculosis superimposed on silica-induced lung disease; extrapulmonary sites are not consistently affected.
Congenital collagen VI myopathy with weakness, contractures and joint hypermobility. Respiratory muscle weakness does not establish intrinsic lung damage.
Skeletal and ectodermal dysplasia; hepatic injury in 5/5 and hydrocephalus in 3/3. Cardiac abnormalities and probable renal concentrating defects omitted under cap.
NRAS-mutated acute myeloid leukemia is a malignant blood and marrow disorder; mutation does not establish additional organ damage.
GRK1-related retinal phototransduction disorder causing congenital stationary night blindness.
Malignant germ-cell tumor of the uterine cervix, a reproductive organ outside the axes.
Site-defined malignancy of the labia minora, a reproductive structure; the broad skin-cancer parent does not specify a separate cutaneous origin.
Dopamine transporter dysfunction causes developmental impairment and parkinsonism-dystonia. Feeding and eye-movement abnormalities do not establish separate organ damage.
Leukoencephalopathy with developmental delay, regression, movement abnormalities and seizures; gastrointestinal and urinary findings occur in 1/9.
Glycosylation disorder; brain atrophy, neuropathy and developmental impairment in 1/1; reduced bone density, scoliosis and hip subluxation in 1/1. Evidence is one patient.
Myopathy, Paget bone disease and frontotemporal degeneration define the syndrome. Cardiac, hepatic and ocular damage are occasional, below 30%.
Brain malformations and hydrocephalus in 13/13; polydactyly is a defining named skeletal feature despite occurring in only 2/13. Other organ frequencies are unestablished.
Defining hypopigmentation, neurodevelopmental disease and hepatomegaly in 2/2; renal structural abnormality in 1/2. Reduced vision in 1/2 omitted under cap; tiny cohort.
Tumor originates in anal canal. Liver findings lack established infiltration or functional damage; pulmonary carcinoid is a separate tumor. Carcinoid syndrome is very rare.
Defining brain disease and cardiomyopathy, present in 4/5; syndactyly in 3/5 and scoliosis in 2/5 support skeletal involvement. Eye-movement signs lack intrinsic eye damage.
Defined by microcephaly and intellectual disability with macrotia, an external-ear structural abnormality; hearing impairment is not established.
Isolated congenital facial nerve dysfunction; orbicularis weakness and reduced corneal reflex do not establish intrinsic ocular disease.
Pancytopenia and occlusive vascular disease directly define blood-cell and vascular involvement; no other organ damage is established.
Four-limb postaxial polydactyly and progressive myopia define the syndrome, both in 80-99%. Hernias do not establish bowel damage; cryptorchidism is outside the axes.
